findings.source_passage: Never did any woman better deserve her name, which was Charity—Aunt Charity, as everybody called her. And like a sister of charity did this charitable Aunt Charity bustle about hither and thither
findings.why_it_matters: The rhetorical triple-play on 'Charity'—her name, the social role, the moral virtue—is Melville's comic wordplay at its most deliberate; the draft reduces her to a list of errands and loses the punning eulogy entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence 'Never did any woman better deserve her name, which was Charity' and at least a clause echoing 'like a sister of charity … bustle about hither and thither' before listing her provisions.

findings.source_passage: Every one knows what a multitude of things—beds, sauce-pans, knives and forks, shovels and tongs, napkins, nut-crackers, and what not, are indispensable to the business of housekeeping.
findings.why_it_matters: The comic catalogue of domestic objects is Ishmael's signature digressive irony—domesticating the epic voyage—and sets up the 'spare Captain and duplicate ship' punch-line whose full force depends on the absurdist buildup that precedes it.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the opening sentence of the housekeeping digression (the catalogue of mundane items) before the compressed whaling-housekeeping analogy.

findings.source_passage: But when a man suspects any wrong, it sometimes happens that if he be already involved in the matter, he insensibly strives to cover up his suspicions even from himself.
findings.source_locator: final full paragraph, reflection on Ahab
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence is a key moment of psychological self-analysis—critics treat it as Ishmael's first admission of unconscious complicity in the voyage's dangers; the draft's paraphrase ('involved men sometimes cover their suspicions from themselves') strips the careful first-person interiority and the moral-philosophical register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore close to verbatim: 'when a man suspects any wrong … if he be already involved in the matter, he insensibly strives to cover up his suspicions even from himself'—this must retain the first-person framing and the word 'insensibly.'

findings.source_passage: she herself owned a score or two of well-saved dollars
findings.source_locator: paragraph 5, closing clause on Aunt Charity
findings.why_it_matters: The ironic deflation—charity motivated partly by a 'score or two of well-saved dollars'—is a small but characteristic Melvillean jab at Quaker mercantilism that enriches the portrait and is wholly missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the parenthetical about her owning 'a score or two of well-saved dollars' in the Aunt Charity passage.

summary: Three medium-severity failures—erasure of the rhetorical triple-play on 'Charity,' loss of the domestic-catalogue setup for the 'spare Captain' joke, and flattening of Ishmael's first-person complicity analysis—collectively cross the regeneration threshold.
